plan.title: Ileum Crohn's vs control: hallmark signature scores per sample
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 ileum samples (6 Crohn disease inflamed, 6 control), raw gene-level Salmon counts (12000 genes x 12 samples), single batch, unpaired. The research question asks for a per-sample score for every MSigDB Hallmark signature and a test of which signatures differ between inflamed and control. Per the grounded procedure: first run sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to characterize sample_01's ~4x-below-median depth without silently dropping it (R-0033, R-0008); then apply a minimal low-count pre-filter and compute DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors plus a blind VST for the scoring input (R-0029, R-0002, R-0026, R-0030) — normalization does not remove sample_01, its lower depth is reflected honestly as wider uncertainty, not exclusion; then score all 50 Hallmark gene sets per sample with UCell's rank-based method, which is depth-invariant and thus robust to the shallow sample (R-0133); then test each of the 50 signature scores between inflamed and control with a linear model (t-test equivalent, two-group unpaired, no covariates) with Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the 50 signatures (R-0134); finally assemble a reproducibility-documented report (versions, gene set version, QC caveats) (R-0086). Human MSigDB Hallmark gene sets (50 sets, HGNC symbols) are confirmed present in the reference store.

steps.method: vst(blind) PCA, sample distance heatmap, library size QC
Keep genes with >=10 counts in >= smallest group size
DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors, vst for scoring input
UCell rank-based per-sample scores on Hallmark gene sets (vst expression)
limma moderated t-test on UCell hallmark scores between inflamed and control, BH across 50 signatures
Reproducibility record: sessionInfo, seed, package versions, gene set collection version
